translations.text: In the second year of King Darius, in the sixth month, on the first day of the month, the word of the LORD came through Haggai the prophet to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, saying:
This is what the Lord Almighty says: These people say, “The time has not come for the Lord’s house to be rebuilt.”
Then the word of the Lord came through Haggai the prophet, saying:
Is this a time for you to live in your roofed houses while this house lies in ruins?
Now this is what the Lord Almighty says: Consider your ways carefully.
You sow much but gather little. You eat but are not satisfied. You drink but do not have enough. You put on clothes but are not warm. Whoever among you earns wages earns them for a bag full of holes.
This is what the Lord Almighty says: Consider your ways carefully.
Go up to the mountain, bring timber, and rebuild this house. I will take pleasure in it and be glorified in it, says the Lord.
You look for much, but it amounts to little. You bring it into the house, but I blow it away. Why is this? says the LORD. Because my house lies in ruins while each of you runs to his own house.
Because of you, the heavens have withheld their dew, and the earth has withheld its produce.
I called for a drought upon the land and the mountains, upon the grain, the wine, and the oil, upon everything the land produces, upon people and livestock, and upon all the labor of your hands.

Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and all the rest of the people obeyed the voice of the LORD their God and the words of Haggai the prophet, whom the LORD their God had sent to them. And the people feared the LORD.
Then Haggai, the Lord’s messenger, spoke to the people with the Lord’s message: “I am with you, says the Lord Almighty.”

The LORD stirred up the spirit of Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, the spirit of Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and the spirit of all the rest of the people. They went and worked on the house of the LORD Almighty, their God.
On the twenty-fourth day of the sixth month, in the second year of King Darius.
On the twenty-first day of the seventh month, the word of the Lord came through Haggai the prophet, saying:
Speak to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and to all the rest of the people:
Who is left among you who saw this house in its former glory? And how do you see it now? Does it not seem like nothing in your eyes?

But now be strong, Zerubbabel, says the LORD. Be strong, Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest. Be strong, all you people of the land, says the LORD, and work, because I am with you, says the LORD Almighty.
The promise I made to you when you came out of Egypt—my Spirit remains among you. Do not be afraid.
For this is what the Lord Almighty says: Once again I will shake the heavens and the earth, the sea and the dry land.
I will shake all the nations, and they will bring the precious things of all the nations. I will fill this house with glory, says the LORD Almighty.
The silver is mine, and the gold is mine, says the Lord Almighty.
The glory of this latter house will be much greater than that of the former, says the LORD Almighty. And in this place I will give my peace, says the LORD Almighty.
On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, in the second year of Darius, the word of the LORD came through Haggai the prophet, saying:
This is what the Lord says: Ask the priests about the law.
If a man carries holy meat in the fold of his cloak, and with that fold touches bread, stew, wine, oil, or any other food, can it become holy? The priests answered, “No.”
Haggai said, “If someone who is himself unclean touches any of these things, does it not become unclean?” The priests answered him, “It becomes unclean.”
Haggai answered, “So it is with this people, and so it is with this nation before me, says the LORD. So it is with all the work of their hands, and whatever they offer there is unclean.”
Now, from this day onward, consider how things were before one stone was laid on another in the LORD’s temple.
When you came to a heap of twenty, there were ten; and when you came to a winepress for fifty, there were twenty.
I struck you and all the work of your hands with scorching heat, mildew, and hail, yet you did not turn to me, says the LORD.
Now devote your hearts to this, from this day onward—from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, from the day when the foundation of the LORD’s temple was laid. Take it to heart.
There is no seed on the threshing floor, and the vine, the fig tree, the pomegranate trees, and the olive trees have not borne fruit. But from today I will bless them, says the LORD.
The word of the LORD came to Haggai a second time, on the twenty-fourth day of the month, saying:
“Tell Zerubbabel, governor of Judah: I will shake the heavens and the earth.

I will overthrow the throne of kingdoms and destroy the strength of the kingdoms of the nations. I will overturn chariots upon their riders, and horses and their riders will fall, each by his brother’s sword.
On that day, says the LORD Almighty, I will take you, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, my servant, says the LORD, and make you like a signet ring, because I have chosen you, says the LORD Almighty.
